question: What is the primary function of Alt + Tab in most modern operating systems?

options.text: Opens a new tab in the current application

solution:
The correct answer is __**Switches between open applications**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Alt + Tab** keyboard shortcut is widely used to **switch between open applications** in modern operating systems like Windows, macOS, and Linux.
 
• Pressing **Alt + Tab** displays a task switcher interface, showing thumbnails or icons of currently running applications.
 
• Users can **hold the Alt key** and repeatedly press Tab to cycle through the open applications.
 
• This feature improves **productivity and multitasking** by allowing quick navigation between multiple tasks without using the mouse.
 
• It is supported by most graphical user interfaces (GUIs) and is a fundamental feature of modern operating systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Task Switcher:**

 
 
• The Task Switcher is a graphical interface activated by **Alt + Tab**, displaying all running applications for easy navigation.
 
• It allows users to preview minimized or background applications before switching to them.
 
 
 
• **Alt + Shift + Tab:**
 
 
• This variation of the shortcut allows users to cycle through open applications in the **reverse order**.
 
• It is useful for quickly returning to the previous application without scrolling through all open tasks.
 
 
 
• **Other Useful Shortcuts:**
 
 
• **Ctrl + Tab:** Switches between tabs within the same application (e.g., in web browsers or text editors).
 
• **Windows + Tab:** Opens the Task View interface in Windows, providing a broader overview of open applications and virtual desktops.
 
 
 
• **Cross-Platform Usage:**
 
 
• While **Alt + Tab** is commonly associated with Windows, macOS uses **Command + Tab** for similar functionality.
 
• Linux-based systems also support **Alt + Tab**, depending on the desktop environment (e.g., GNOME, KDE).
